meta.notes: TUSCANY CROSSING 103K CYCLE - nutrition (rev 2.0). 29 weeks, 9/28/2026 -> 4/18/2027, matched to run_plan / strength_plan rev 2.0 subtypes. Arnon: 50 M, 175 lb / 79 kg. || THE PROBLEM TO SOLVE (FR-w): at Vermont the gut signalled FULL at ~365 cal/hr by hour 4 (gels every 25 min + half-strength drink + 500 ml/hr); he then ran on gels alone at ~240 cal/hr with no energy cost to 6:40. Tuscany is a ~15:40-17:00 planning day. The fix is the calorie MIX - more solids, less concentrated liquid carbohydrate - not more volume. Target race intake ~260-300 cal/hr, from ~50% gels / ~25% half-strength drink / ~25% real food. || GUT-TRAINING LADDER (long_run notes + overrides): Base W3-13 proven protocol + one real-food item per long run from W7 | Build W14-22 the MIX at 250-280 cal/hr, cup drinking at car stops | Oracle 1/30 = J-2, the real-food and aid-station rehearsal on an ~11 h day | Peak: race protocol v1 on 3/7, final on 3/21, nothing new after. One new variable per run; hour 1 always on the proven baseline. || STATION FLUID vs OWN MIX (Arnon's question): with powder pre-portioned per bottle, mixing your own at a cup-only aid costs roughly 20-40 s more than taking station drink - small next to the dwell Vermont actually lost (~4 min of crew chat and toilet queue). The bigger variable is the gut: the station product at Tuscany is unknown (race documents should list it - open item), and your own mix is proven over two ultras. DEFAULT: own powder + station water; station coke/tea/broth as late-race additions only after they pass in training. Tested head-to-head at Oracle (one timed aid, one-hour gut read). || SODIUM & FLUID BY TEMPERATURE (not a flat rate): < 12 C -> 400-600 mg Na/hr, 400-500 ml/hr (no scheduled SaltStick) | 12-22 C -> 600-800 mg, 500-650 ml (SaltStick 1/60 min) | > 22 C -> 800-1,000 mg, 650-800 ml (SaltStick 1/40-45 min). Tuscany's regulation warns of near 0 C at night and > 30 C midday. || EARLY-START FUELING: Tuscany breakfast lands at ~02:45-03:00. Rehearsed on 11/15 (04:00) and 2/21 (03:00, identical to race timing). || CAFFEINE for a dark finish: tested at dusk on 1/10, then at Oracle and in the March rehearsals; race cap ~5 mg/kg (~400 mg). || DAILY EATING: protein 1.8-1.9 g/kg (~145-155 g) every day including rest days - tendon remodeling at 50 is protein-hungry. Carbs scale with the day (~3.3 g/kg rest -> ~8 g/kg on the biggest long runs; day-type phase_adjustments raise totals as hours climb from ~6 to ~13 run h/week). ENERGY AVAILABILITY: weekly hours roughly double from October to March - if body weight drifts down > ~1.5 kg, or sleep, mood or resting HR worsen, eat more before training less. COLLAGEN 15 g + vitamin C 250 mg 30-60 min before every Lower A/B session, otherwise with the morning foot routine. NO NSAIDs around loading. Alcohol: Friday evening is the window in normal weeks (36 h before a Sunday long run); none in the Oracle or Tuscany race weeks. || AeT TESTS: nutrition is held identical at every drift test (10/13, 11/24, 1/5, 2/16) so the only variable is fitness. || SWIM DAYS (rev 2.1): three day types resolve Total Immersion swim days (Monday swim-only; Friday swim + Upper B, with or without an easy run). They are listed FIRST because triggers are first-match: a trigger with cross_subtype matches only when that cross session is scheduled; a trigger without cross_subtype ignores cross sessions (backward compatible). Easy swim ~250-400 kcal. || date_overrides are the source of truth on test, gate, headlamp, rehearsal, carb-load and race days.

daily_targets.notes: FUELING LADDER (FR-w: the problem is calorie MIX, not volume). BASE W3-13: proven gels every 25-30 min + water, 200-250 cal/hr; from W7 add ONE real-food item at ~hour 2 on runs >= 2.5 h, rotating (salted boiled potato, rice ball, 1/4 PB&J, banana, bread + cheese). BUILD W14-22: 250-280 cal/hr as a MIX - gels ~50%, half-strength drink ~25%, real food ~25% every 45-60 min - so no single source runs over ~150 cal/hr (Vermont's fullness came at ~365 cal/hr, mostly gel + drink). PEAK W23-26: race protocol v1 (overrides 3/7, 3/21). One new variable per run; hour 1 always on the proven baseline.

supplements.name: Vitamin D3
supplements.notes: Autumn blood work suggested (25-OH vitamin D, ferritin, CBC) before the winter volume block - dose by result. Do not supplement iron without a low ferritin result.

supplements.name: Omega-3 fish oil (EPA/DHA)
supplements.rationale: Anti-inflammatory support without blunting adaptation (unlike NSAIDs, which stay OFF around loading).

supplements.name: Collagen peptides + Vitamin C
supplements.timing: 30-60 min BEFORE lower/tendon strength sessions; on non-lifting days, with the morning foot-corrective block
supplements.rationale: Peri-loading collagen availability for tendon remodeling — the P1 nutritional lever. Daily low-dose beats one big weekly dose because collagen synthesis has a refractory window.
supplements.notes: THE priority supplement this block. Never skipped on Lower A / Lower B days.

supplements.name: Creatine monohydrate
supplements.timing: post-run or post-strength, any consistent daily slot
supplements.rationale: Strength/power support during the HSR block; consistency matters more than timing.

supplements.name: Whey protein isolate
supplements.timing: post-session windows and to top up daily protein
supplements.rationale: Hits the 1.7-1.9 g/kg/day protein target that tissue remodeling at 50 demands.

supplements.name: Magnesium glycinate
supplements.rationale: Sleep quality — recovery is the P1 multiplier.

supplements.name: Electrolytes (SaltStick)
supplements.dose: Temperature-tiered: < 12 C none scheduled (gel + mix cover it); 12-22 C 1 capsule/60 min; > 22 C 1 capsule/40-45 min
supplements.rationale: Vermont sodium (515-675 mg/hr) was deliberately low for 56 F and caused no cramping; Tuscany's 0-30 C swing needs a tiered rate, not a flat one.

supplements.name: Caffeine (GU Roctane caffeine gels)
supplements.dose: 35 mg per caffeinated gel. Training runs > 3 h: 1-3 in the final third. Evening/dark sessions: one at dusk (test). Race: see the 4/17 override (<= ~400 mg total).
supplements.timing: Final third of long efforts; dusk on headlamp runs
supplements.rationale: Vermont: 3 caffeinated gels in the last 2.5 h, clean. Tuscany adds a 15-17 h day and a dark finish - timing is tested on 1/10, 1/30, 3/7, 3/21.
